title: Injury Risk: Injured, Recovering and Chronic Cases
markdown:
**Summary.** Separate three groups before the 2026-10-18 auction. Chronic same-spot lower-body cases (degenerative knees, repeated foot, ankle or calf problems, mystery illness) get bid below their per-game value, and you should own only a few of them. One-off injuries from last season can be bought with more confidence than their ADP suggests. Only players tagged O can use our 4 IL slots right away, so Q-tagged injured players take up a real roster spot until their tag changes.

## The rules that matter for us

Not every injury counts the same. Be cautious with players who have repeated injuries or surgeries to the same lower-body part, especially knees, and with anyone who has an ongoing mystery illness. Hand, finger, shoulder and oblique injuries do not matter much. Concussions matter a little. So a shoulder surgery or a broken thumb last season is not a reason to lower your bid. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873))

Chronic cases get priced down even after a healthy year. A good season from a player with a degenerative injury does not remove the risk. Repeated surgeries or problems in the same spot make future missed time more likely. In our auction, that means you stop bidding below the player's per-game value, not at it. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=380), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547))

Do not stack injury risks. Before you bid on a risky player, count how many big risks you already own. Keep that count on your draft sheet. Once you have one or two chronic cases among your expensive players, pass on the next one unless the price falls well below his value. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1769), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1343))

## Chronic cases: price them down

The clearest chronic cases in our pool are knees. Kawhi Leonard has a degenerative knee with repeated meniscus, ACL and quad tendinopathy surgeries, and Toronto is expected to manage his load. Joel Embiid has had multiple meniscus surgeries on the same knee, does not play back-to-backs and is projected for 49 to 54 games. Stephen Curry's runner's knee is a wear-and-tear issue he calls a new normal, and he played 43 games last season. Per game, all three are much better than their price. That gap is the chronic discount working as intended. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547), [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331), [Joel Embiid](#player/165), [Stephen Curry](#player/124))

The same rule covers other same-spot histories. Zach Edey has had repeated foot and ankle surgeries. Coby White has had four calf strains in 12 months. Darius Garland has persistent toe and knee problems. Donovan Mitchell, Karl-Anthony Towns, Kyrie Irving and Paul George all carry long knee histories, and Giannis Antetokounmpo adds calf injuries to persistent knee problems. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547), [Zach Edey](#player/158), [Coby White](#player/594), [Darius Garland](#player/185), [Donovan Mitchell](#player/391), [Karl-Anthony Towns](#player/560), [Kyrie Irving](#player/259), [Paul George](#player/189), [Giannis Antetokounmpo](#player/19))

Back-to-back counts matter mostly for injury-prone players, so check them for these names. Dallas has 16 back-to-backs, the most in the league, and Kyrie Irving is expected to sit them, especially early. Boston also has 16, and Paul George is expected to sit about 8 to 10. Golden State has 15 for Curry. Philadelphia has three in our playoff weeks, which likely cuts Embiid to about 8 games in weeks 19 to 21. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1686), [Kyrie Irving](#player/259), [Paul George](#player/189), [Stephen Curry](#player/124), [Joel Embiid](#player/165))

## One-off injuries and returns: do not overreact

Drafters are too scared of players coming back from injuries that cost them last season. You can bid with more confidence than their ADPs suggest. Nikola Jokić played 65 games with a knee injury, Anthony Edwards 61, and Domantas Sabonis was healthy and played in the preseason after a 19-game season. Walker Kessler's shoulder surgery falls in the group of injuries that do not matter much. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1258), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873), [Nikola Jokić](#player/288), [Anthony Edwards](#player/160), [Domantas Sabonis](#player/491), [Walker Kessler](#player/310))

Returns still have a hidden cost. Players coming back from injury usually have minutes limits and miss back-to-backs, so all of their numbers drop while they ramp up. Tyrese Haliburton is expected to play about 30 minutes in games without a back-to-back after missing all of 2025-26. Fred VanVleet starts near 30 minutes and should rise to about 34. Damian Lillard is expected to sit back-to-backs, mostly early. Expect weaker early weeks from them and check their minutes in October and November. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1700), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386), [Tyrese Haliburton](#player/215), [Fred VanVleet](#player/570), [Damian Lillard](#player/334))

For players hurt right now, avoid the ones who start the season injured, but remember the season is 25 weeks long. A short-term injury should lower the bid a little, not wipe it out. On draft day, 2026-10-18, check the Yahoo tags for Bam Adebayo (groin), Chet Holmgren (quadriceps, plus a reported hip issue), Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Dejounte Murray (toe) and Nic Claxton (hamstring). If one of them goes cheap because of the tag, that is a buy, not a trap. ([09-27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=561), [Bam Adebayo](#player/4), [Chet Holmgren](#player/243), [Kon Knueppel](#player/315), [Dejounte Murray](#player/399), [Nic Claxton](#player/105))

## Where the experts disagree

The notes pull in two directions on players coming back from injury. One side says drafters are too scared of last season's injuries, and you can be more confident than ADP suggests. The other side says a healthy year does not erase a degenerative problem, repeated same-spot injuries make more missed time likely, and returning players lose value to minutes limits and missed back-to-backs. The two views fit together if you sort by type. Use the confident view for one-off injuries such as a broken bone or a single surgery. Use the cautious view for same-spot repeats and degenerative knees. The player notes show the same split. LaMelo Ball has repeated ankle injuries, but the experts call those fears overblown. Jalen Green had three hamstring strains in 2025-26, and the experts call the hamstring not a concern now. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1258), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=380), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1700), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386), [LaMelo Ball](#player/27), [Jalen Green](#player/208))

## Using our 4 IL slots

Yahoo removed IL+. A player tagged out or injured can go on IL right away. Questionable, doubtful and probable players cannot. This matters for draft-day picks. Ingram, Butler, Konan Niederhäuser and Porziņģis are tagged O, so they can move to IL at once and free a roster spot for a waiver add. Coby White, Bam Adebayo, Chet Holmgren and even Dereck Lively II, who has a broken foot but a Yahoo Q (Foot) tag, cannot go on IL until their tag changes. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292), [Brandon Ingram](#player/257), [Jimmy Butler III](#player/78), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](#player/417), [Kristaps Porziņģis](#player/453), [Coby White](#player/594), [Dereck Lively II](#player/335))

Do not draft or stash a long-term injured player as a plan. Only keep him in an empty IL slot and drop him once you need the spot. The experts split on Brandon Ingram, who is out with a partially torn Achilles and expected back between Thanksgiving and Christmas. One expert calls him fine around picks 100 to 110 in stash formats. Others avoid him inside the top 120. With 4 IL slots, he is a reasonable last-round bench pick for a team with a free slot. Jimmy Butler (ACL, about January) and Konan Niederhäuser (foot, around Christmas) are 1 USD final picks only if an IL slot is free. ([09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2182), [Brandon Ingram](#player/257), [Jimmy Butler III](#player/78), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](#player/417))

Some injured players are not worth an IL slot. Hukporti, Veesaar and Quaintance may miss the whole season. Saunders is expected back only near the end of his rookie season, likely after our 2027-03-28 finish. Mark Williams, Shaedon Sharpe, Moses Moody and Donte DiVincenzo are out until around March. Track their news in February as waiver adds for weeks 19 to 21 instead of holding them all winter. Porziņģis has no return date and an ongoing mystery illness, so the safer play is to leave him on waivers. ([09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2182), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873), [Ariel Hukporti](#player/250), [Henri Veesaar](#player/572), [Jayden Quaintance](#player/465), [Richie Saunders](#player/727), [Mark Williams](#player/608), [Shaedon Sharpe](#player/510), [Moses Moody](#player/395), [Donte DiVincenzo](#player/144), [Kristaps Porziņģis](#player/453))
